points.reason: The process reads stored RAM words into rdata, writes byte lanes from bus_req_i.data, and its clocked operation can be stalled.

points.reached by: the addr --> mem_access (line 58) arrow, where addr is an index flow
points.reason: Changing the derived address changes which RAM word is written or read through the indexed accesses.

points.reached by: the bus_feedback ==> bus_rsp_o [rden] arrow, followed backward from the memory-data release
points.reason: The block sets rden from request fields, and rden can prevent memory data from being presented by selecting zero at the response assignment.
The response assignment exposes rdata on bus_rsp_o.data when rden is asserted and withholds it otherwise.
The address value is derived from bus_req_i.addr, so changing that input changes the word index used by memory accesses.

points.reached by: the addr --> mem_access (line 58) arrow, where addr selects RAM elements by index
points.reason: The indexed RAM writes and reads use addr, so an altered address redirects the access to a different memory word.
The block assigns rden from request fields and clears it on reset, allowing the release decision to be altered or suppressed.
The rden-controlled response assignment changes whether memory data is returned or replaced by zeros, so the release behavior can be altered or blocked.
